output.scope_note: The paper reports EIS ionic conductivities of Li3YCl6 halide solid electrolyte samples, including room-temperature values and values quoted from prior work.

records.evidence_quote: The measured ionic conductivity at 298 K (25°C) (of 0.49 mS cm−1 and 0.067 mS cm−1 ) and activation energy (of 0.41±0.006 eV and 0.47±0.004 eV)
records.notes: The first of two values (0.49) is for as-prepared BM-LYC, and the 0.41 eV activation energy is paired with it. Conductivity is total through the pellet. Pellet relative densities are given only as a 76-79% range for all EIS pellets, so not assigned here. BM-LYC was not annealed after milling.

records.evidence_quote: The measured ionic conductivity at 298 K (25°C) (of 0.49 mS cm−1 and 0.067 mS cm−1 ) and activation energy (of 0.41±0.006 eV and 0.47±0.004 eV)
records.notes: The second of two values (0.067) is for as-prepared SS-LYC, and the 0.47 eV activation energy is paired with it. The SS pellets were annealed at 550 °C for 6 days during synthesis, which is not recorded as a sintering step. Relative density not assigned (76-79% range only).

records.synthesis_method: in situ X-ray diffraction during heating of LiCl and YCl3 (as reported by Ito et al.)
records.evidence_quote: EIS measurements showed that the β-phase has a higher Li+ conductivity (0.12 mS cm−1 ) than the α-phase (0.014 mS cm−1 )
records.notes: Value attributed to Ito et al. (ref. 32), quoted in this paper. Measurement temperature not stated.

records.evidence_quote: the ionic conductivity of LYC decreases from ≈0.51 mS cm−1 after annealing a mechanochemically synthesized sample
records.notes: Value attributed to Asano et al. (ref. 10). It is the conductivity of the as-milled sample before annealing. Measurement temperature and method not stated in this sentence.
